raw_response:
I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the system I trust most because it fits the climate, the irrigation conditions, and what I know how to manage well. I care more about steady yield and lower risk than chasing something fancy, so I will not switch into cash crops this year. I will plant winter wheat on all my land, then after harvest I will plant summer maize on the same fields. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most fertilizer down as base plus a topdressing at jointing, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for weeds, aphids, and disease. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into hybrid summer maize, keep the stand uniform, use less irrigation than wheat, and focus on one or two timely spray rounds if pests or disease pressure show up. I will manage costs tightly, avoid excessive fertilizer, and aim for reliable production rather than the highest possible input level.
